I have resolved the issue where email messages crashed on non-ASCII domain names when email encoding is set to a non-unicode charset (e.g. `iso-8859-1`).

### Cause
When the machine hostname contains non-ASCII characters or when `DNS_NAME` contains unicode characters, `email.utils.make_msgid(domain=DNS_NAME)` returns a `Message-ID` header containing non-ASCII domain characters. When message encoding is non-unicode (e.g. `iso-8859-1`), header encoding fails with `UnicodeEncodeError` because `Message-ID` headers are not address headers and cannot be encoded via MIME header encoding. RFC 5322 requires IDN domain names in email headers to be represented in IDNA / punycode ASCII format.

### Solution
1. In [`django/core/mail/utils.py`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-5lyurmnk/django/core/mail/utils.py#L14-L21), updated `CachedDnsName.get_fqdn()` to convert `socket.getfqdn()` to IDNA ASCII (punycode) if it contains non-ASCII characters.
2. In [`django/core/mail/message.py`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-5lyurmnk/django/core/mail/message.py#L114-L123), wrapped `make_msgid()` to convert the `domain` parameter (or `DNS_NAME` fallback) to IDNA ASCII (punycode) if non-ASCII characters are present.
3. Added test cases in [`tests/mail/tests.py`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-5lyurmnk/tests/mail/tests.py#L407-L417) to verify that `Message-ID` generation and `CachedDnsName` properly handle unicode DNS names.
